title: Logical functions: putting the pieces together

screens.prompt: In B9, put PASS in the cell when the total is over 100 and no item is under 15 units, otherwise FAIL.

hints.syntax: =IF(AND(test 1, test 2),"PASS","FAIL"): the tests sit inside the IF, in brackets of their own.
hints.func-if: The cell has to say PASS or FAIL, so the combined test needs an IF around it.
hints.func-and: Both conditions have to hold at once, and only AND does that.
hints.require-ref: Read the total from B8 and the units from B2:B7.
hints.value: 150 clears the total test and 18 clears the floor, so B9 reads PASS.
hints.error: A division by zero inside a test gives #DIV/0!, so the verdict never appears.

reject.why: that answers TRUE instead of the word PASS
one test cannot hold both conditions, and the words are the wrong way round
the smallest item is 18, so a 20-unit floor answers FAIL
the total is recalculated instead of reading the total row
text divided by zero leaves #VALUE! in the cell
the missing comma merges two tests into one argument

screens.prompt: In D8, average the price column and round it to one decimal, but say none when there is nothing to average.

hints.func-if: A number or the word none is two outcomes, which is what IF is for.
hints.func-isnumber: ISNUMBER is the guard: it asks whether the average produced a number at all.
hints.func-round: ROUND sets one decimal place; the cell format would only change how 4.3166 looks.
hints.value: The six prices come to 25.9, which is 4.3166 each, so one decimal place gives 4.3.
hints.error: The finished value is divided by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0! and the guard never gets a chance.

reject.why: that answers 4.32 with no guard and no second outcome
a magnitude test is not a guard against an empty range, and 4.3 fails it
the average is left unrounded at 4.3166
two decimal places answer 4.32 instead of 4.3
the range starts on row 3, so the first price is left out
the finished value is then divided by zero
the missing comma leaves the IF with a test and one argument

docs.explain:
The two formulas here put the earlier pieces together. The first nests AND inside IF: both tests are checked and the cell answers PASS or FAIL rather than TRUE or FALSE. The second wraps an average in ISNUMBER before rounding it, so a price column with no numbers returns none instead of an error.

On the first screen the total is 150 and the smallest item is 18, so both tests hold and B9 reads PASS. The second screen averages six prices to 4.3166 and rounds that to 4.3. Every figure comes from the grid, so a corrected price moves the answer without the formula changing.

ROUND changes the value while cell formatting changes only the look, so a rounded figure can be summed and a formatted one still carries its decimals underneath. A guard on the calculation names the condition that could fail, which reads better than IFERROR over the whole formula.

errors.text: The finished text result was used in arithmetic, as when PASS is divided by zero.
AVERAGE found no numbers in C2:C7 and divided a zero total by a count of zero.
One of the nested function names was mistyped, so the whole formula fails.

docs.atWork: Printing a rounded average with a word in place of an error when a month has no data.
docs.outcome: Combine a logical test, a combined test and a rounded calculation in one formula.
docs.teaches: nesting AND inside IF, and guarding a calculation with ISNUMBER before ROUND
docs.dataset: Stock list with a total row, and a price column to average

seo.title: Combine IF, AND and ROUND in Excel
seo.description: Nest AND inside IF and the cell answers PASS or FAIL instead of TRUE. Guard the average with ISNUMBER so a text-only column says none instead of #DIV/0!.
